cases.caption: Historical first-rebound restitution for pfc-linear-restitution-md0-beta02. Panel (a) compares the retained first-apex height estimator $e_h=\sqrt{\max(z_{\mathrm{apex}}-R,0)/(z_{\mathrm{initial}}-R)}$ with the public PFC $M_d=0$ contact target $e_0=\exp[-\pi\beta/\sqrt{1-\beta^2}]$ for $0\leq\beta<1$, with $e_0=0$ at $\beta=1$ (black solid analytical curve or horizontal line). Panel (b) shows absolute coefficient errors and the strict published absolute-error limit 0.01 (black dashed line). Panel (c) shows relative discrepancy as a separate diagnostic, not the acceptance criterion. Blue open circles, orange crosses, green open squares and purple plus signs denote CPU at $\Delta t$, GPU at $\Delta t$, CPU at $\Delta t/2$ and GPU at $\Delta t/2$, respectively; all numerical observations are unconnected symbols, and coincident runs remain overlaid without averaging or jitter. $\Delta t=10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s}$; $\Delta t/2=5\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{s}$. Only four summary observations exist at $\beta=0.2$; the horizontal categories do not form a time history. All three ordinates are linear and exact zeros retain their true value. PFC was not executed locally: the reference is its published analytical relation, not a PFC numerical trajectory. The historical PASS records absolute-error acceptance only and does not imply small relative error at strong damping.

Historical first-rebound restitution for pfc-linear-restitution-md0-sweep. Panel (a) compares the retained first-apex height estimator $e_h=\sqrt{\max(z_{\mathrm{apex}}-R,0)/(z_{\mathrm{initial}}-R)}$ with the public PFC $M_d=0$ contact target $e_0=\exp[-\pi\beta/\sqrt{1-\beta^2}]$ for $0\leq\beta<1$, with $e_0=0$ at $\beta=1$ (black solid analytical curve or horizontal line). Panel (b) shows absolute coefficient errors and the strict published absolute-error limit 0.01 (black dashed line). Panel (c) shows relative discrepancy as a separate diagnostic, not the acceptance criterion. Blue open circles, orange crosses, green open squares and purple plus signs denote CPU at $\Delta t$, GPU at $\Delta t$, CPU at $\Delta t/2$ and GPU at $\Delta t/2$, respectively; all numerical observations are unconnected symbols, and coincident runs remain overlaid without averaging or jitter. $\Delta t=10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s}$; $\Delta t/2=5\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{s}$. Sixteen independent damping ratios are retained per run. Relative discrepancy is undefined at $e_0=0$ ($\beta=1$) and that point is omitted only from (c); the largest plotted relative discrepancy is 100.000%. At $\beta=0.9$ and $\beta=1$, the retained $e_h=0$ denotes non-rebound. The recorded extremum at $\beta=0.9$ is below the nominal radius and is clamped to zero by the height estimator; $\beta=1$ has no recorded apex, so its retained zero is a non-rebound convention rather than an observed apex-height measurement. The black analytical curve is an evaluation of the stated closed-form equation, not interpolation of the numerical observations. All three ordinates are linear and exact zeros retain their true value. PFC was not executed locally: the reference is its published analytical relation, not a PFC numerical trajectory. The historical PASS records absolute-error acceptance only and does not imply small relative error at strong damping.
